beats.subject: a hand plants flat on the floor
beats.note: Start on a detail, not the person. The audience is oriented by an object, so the next shot can be disorienting without losing them.

beats.subject: the face upside down, holding still
beats.note: MOTION 4.9 - this is a near-still with a whisper of drift. The most striking image in the sequence is the cheapest thing to generate. Buy your best frame here.

beats.subject: the body inverted into a handstand
beats.note: MOTION 2.6, the quietest beat. The calm before the burst; it makes the next two read as fast.

beats.subject: the figure travels away down the corridor
beats.note: MOTION 12.8 - triple the previous beat. The cut INTO this is hidden by the jump in movement. Nobody checks continuity across a spike.

beats.subject: the figure comes back at the lens
beats.note: MOTION 14.7 and the shortest beat at 0.77s. Peak movement, minimum time on screen: the eye cannot audit it.

beats.subject: the subject arrives, gesture toward camera
beats.note: MOTION 9.9, luma easing back. The landing. Let it breathe or the sequence reads as noise.

note: Close-up hook, then an impossible-looking exit assembled from short clips cut on motion.
how_to_use: Each beat is a slot. Put your own character, style and place in it and render each beat as its own clip at the given length, then cut them together in order. The card carries TIMING AND INTENT ONLY - no frame of the reference is in it, and it cannot reconstruct the source.
provenance: Structure measured from a reference the operator supplied. Shot lengths and cut placement are craft, not content - the imagery, characters and design of the source are NOT here and must not be reproduced. Cast it with your own.
craft:
THE ILLUSION IS THE EDIT, NOT THE MODEL. Six clips, none longer than 1.5 seconds, read as one impossible continuous action. Measured shape: three quiet beats (motion 2.6-4.9), then two fast ones (12.8, 14.7), then a settle. Luma climbs 101 -> 121 across the run, so the sequence moves toward light.
Two rules fall out of that and both are free:
  1. CUT ON THE MOTION SPIKE. A cut placed where movement jumps is invisible; the same cut in a calm beat is obvious.
  2. SPEND THE TIME ON THE STILL. The hero shot here barely moves. Generate a great frame, animate it for a second, and stop.
cast_it_with: Any single character who can be shot in close-up, then at a distance, then approaching. No dialogue, no second subject.
verdict: Structure measured and annotated from the contact sheet. NOT yet rendered with our own cast - unproven as a template until it is.
subject_mode_note: insert = no character in the prompt at all; figure = body and action without the face description; face = the full character prose. The first render of this card ignored every framing and action because the character's face prose is a paragraph of nouns and the framing was one token - the model renders nouns, so it drew a face six times.
